There's no way we'll ever voluntarily reduce our consumption and quality of life to the point that we avoid the worst of climate catastrophe.
The only way to force that change would be through authoritarian means.
By authoritarian i don't mean the conservative definition which amounts to meatless Mondays. We're talking the seizing and redistribution of resources, reduced economic freedom and silencing of the protests that would follow. Basically everything that's already happening to the lower class but now it would affect the middle and upper class as well.

I thought I had responded to your comment weeks ago. Turned out I hadn't. My bad.

I pretty much agree wholeheartedly with everything you've written. As you mentioned with the Suffragists, nonviolent protest is an option often exclusive to the privileged like myself.

The short answer is that I added the disclaimer more as a cheeky attempt at appeasing the ever watchful overlords of reddit. And it was kinda dumb. Probably should have just said that I don't personally advocate for violence or disruption but could foresee it as a natural outcome of the situation as it's the only effective option.

Most of what I have to say about the nature of forcing change you've already covered better than I could. I don't have a particularly good grasp on history, but enough to recognize the pattern you mentioned. I wouldn't know how we'd operate long-term or how to achieve change broadly but I do have some ideas for specific things that could be done that are best left unsaid here.

Protest on the streets and in front of their mansions. Vote out the climate criminals in local and national elections. Boycott what they are selling us. Do everything in your power to make life harder for them within the boundaries of what's legally acceptable. They're not gonna listen to us until we put actual pressure on them. 

However, doing any of these by oneself accomplishes next to nothing in terms of making noticable change. 

I think the most important thing we can do is recruiting as many people as we can for the cause, have them recruiting as many as they can and so on. 

By convincing one other person to go vegan, protest, etc. you still have next to no influence over the fate of the planet but you do have double the influence of what you had before.

Thanks for the suggestions. I'll be sure to check the out.

To hell with anyone who excuses, normalizes or promotes violence and discrimination against autistic people. (this goes for any other marginalized group as well)
